name: graphify
description: Turn any codebase, with its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs, into a queryable knowledge graph. A /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI: local deterministic AST parsing, every edge explained, no vector store.
one_liner: A tool that reads an entire codebase — code, docs, configs, PDFs — and turns it into a map you can ask questions of, instead of grepping through files to understand how everything connects.
buyer: An engineering manager onboarding a new hire onto a large, messy, undocumented legacy codebase who needs them productive in days, not months.
business_use_cases: A new engineering hire asks the graph 'what calls this function and why' instead of spending their first two weeks reading code cold.
An engineering team doing acquisition due diligence maps a target company's codebase quickly to assess its real complexity before a deal closes.
A compliance team traces how a sensitive data field flows through a codebase for an audit, using the explained edges instead of manual code review.

money_ideas.idea: Graphify itself already sells a Cloud subscription; an independent angle is 'legacy codebase onboarding' consulting using the free local tool as the first step.

steal_this: Offer a fixed-price 'codebase X-ray' service: run graphify on a client's messy legacy repo and deliver a one-page map plus a written explanation of its riskiest connections, within a week.
